#Air Quality Dataset — North Africa & Mediterranean Basin (2016–2026)
##Overview
This dataset combines ground-truth PM2.5 measurements from the OpenAQ network with satellite and reanalysis features extracted via Google Earth Engine (GEE). It covers monitoring stations in the Mediterranean Basin near Algeria — spanning Spain, Italy, Tunisia, Morocco, and surrounding countries — from November 2016 to April 2026.
The primary use case is building machine learning models to predict surface PM2.5 concentration using remotely-sensed atmospheric and meteorological variables, which is especially valuable for regions like Algeria where ground sensors are sparse.

##Geographic Coverage
ParameterValueRegionMediterranean Basin / North Africa vicinityLatitude range~34.3°N – 43.7°NLongitude range~-5.7°E – 9.4°ECountries coveredSpain, France, Italy, Tunisia, Morocco, and nearby areasGround stations (PM2.5)125 unique sensorsGEE grid locations100 unique IDs

Algeria itself has very limited ground PM2.5 monitoring. This dataset uses the surrounding Mediterranean region — climatically and atmospherically similar — as a proxy training ground for developing models transferable to Algeria.


##Dataset Structure
air-quality-algeria/


- openaq_pm25.csv          # Ground-truth PM2.5 from OpenAQ sensors
- gee_features_daily.csv   # Satellite + reanalysis features from GEE
- combined gee #Cobined csv file based on date , lat , lon

#Intended Use Cases

PM2.5 regression/prediction using satellite-derived features
Transfer learning to estimate air quality in data-scarce regions (e.g., Algeria)
Spatiotemporal analysis of air quality trends in the Mediterranean
Feature importance studies (which of AOD, NO2, wind, temperature best predicts PM2.5?)
Baseline for comparing ML models: XGBoost, Random Forest, LSTMs, or graph-based approaches


 #Data Quality Notes

-PM2.5 outliers: Filter pm25 <= 0 and pm25 >= 500 for realistic values (WHO guideline: 15 µg/m³ annual mean).
Sentinel-5P gaps: NO2, CO, O3 columns are missing on cloudy days (~12% of records). Consider imputation or masking.
-Spatial join: When merging GEE features with PM2.5 ground stations, match on date + nearest lat/lon (e.g., using a threshold of ~0.25°).
-Wind speed: Reconstruct scalar wind speed as sqrt(wind_u² + wind_v²) if direction is not needed.
